references.text: The continuation of the list of women who followed Jesus and served him with their possessions, providing context for Mary Magdalene and the other women.
Mary Magdalene is mentioned among the women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him, and who were present at the crucifixion.
Mary Magdalene is mentioned among the women who followed Jesus and served him while he was in Galilee, and who watched the crucifixion.
Mark confirms that Jesus had driven out seven evil spirits from Mary Magdalene, a direct parallel to Luke's note about the seven demons.
Mary Magdalene is named as one of the women who told the apostles about the empty tomb and the resurrection.
Mary Magdalene was present at Jesus' cross, showing her faithful following from the beginning.
Mary Magdalene was the first to arrive at the tomb on resurrection day and discovered that the stone had been rolled away.
Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene after his resurrection, highlighting her central role among his female followers.
An example of Jesus driving out evil spirits, illustrating the type of healing the women in verse 2 had experienced.
Jesus speaks of seven evil spirits that take up residence in a person, shedding light on the number seven demons that were driven out from Mary Magdalene.
Jesus' teaching about seven evil spirits that are worse than the first, relevant to understanding that Mary Magdalene was freed from seven demons.
